Apple must respond by Monday to a complaint filed by Epic Games with Brazilian antitrust regulators, accusing Apple of making restrictive interpretations of its obligations under a recent App Store antitrust agreement reached in Brazil. Details below.

A little background

Two months ago, Apple announced that it now allows developers to distribute apps through alternative app marketplaces in Brazil.

The change stemmed from a settlement agreement that resolved a years-long antitrust investigation launched after a complaint by Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre over Apple's App Store rules.

Under the new terms, developers in Brazil can distribute iOS apps through alternative app marketplaces with payment methods outside of Apple's IAP system.

Apple also introduced a new commission structure, including a 5% Core Technology Fee on digital goods and services sold for apps distributed outside of the App Store. You can read more about the structure here.

Epic questions Apple's execution

According to Brazilian newspaper O Globo (via MacMagazine) today, Epic recently filed a petition with CADE, Brazil's antitrust regulator, accusing Apple of setting up "structural, technical, and access barriers" that diminish the practical viability of alternative app distribution.

Epic says that although Brazil's new terms apply only to iOS apps, the agreement Apple reached with CADE "clearly covers iPadOS."

According to the report, Epic is also objecting to what it calls "intimidating prompts" that discourage users from installing apps outside of the App Store, as well as to the current installation process, which Epic says requires nine steps, three more than how Apple currently does it in Europe.

O Globo reports that Epic further noted that Apple's original installation process in Europe required 15 steps, but after being ordered to reduce it to six, "download abandonment dropped from 65% to 25%."

Finally, Epic told CADE that Apple's reporting requirements "go well beyond what is necessary to calculate fees" and allow Apple to "monitor competitors' business models."

O Globo says CADE has given Apple until Monday to respond. Apple has not publicly commented on the matter.
